Process: Baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) grown in a fed-batch bioreactor. Biomass concentration x1 and substrate (glucose) concentration x2 are measured every hour, in g/L. The operator sets the dilution rate u1 (1/h) and the substrate concentration in the feed u2 (g/L), both held constant between switches. Three experiments of 20 h with different starting biomass and input profiles. Measurement error is about 5% of the reading plus 0.01 g/L. The growth kinetics are unknown: find the rate law that explains the data.

answer.feedback: No candidate qualifies: every fit exceeds its 95% chi-square limit, and C20, C40, and C17 also have an imprecisely estimated parameter. In the next search, look beyond a single global substrate-rate law for a mechanism that can explain experiment-dependent growth or substrate-consumption dynamics. The best-fitting models (C29/C20) over-predict E1 biomass around 9 h, under-predict E2 substrate early (around 1 h), and over-predict E3 substrate around 7 h. That contrast suggests too much modeled consumption in E2 but too little in E3; consider condition-dependent uptake/yield or a dynamic adaptation effect. The supplied diagnostics do not establish which substrate levels are high or low.
answer.reasoning: C29 has the highest Akaike weight among the near-fitting candidates and all its parameters are precise, but chi-square 148.1 exceeds the 147.7 limit, so it cannot be accepted. C20 is similarly close but its m parameter is not resolved; C9 and the other candidates also fail their fit limits. The small AIC differences do not override the lack of fit.
